evals.expected_output: Diagnoses boolean-flag soup and illegal state combinations, recommends an explicit state machine (State pattern or enum + match, scaled to the problem) with entry/exit handling that fixes the stuck-dash bug, treats hurt as an interrupt transition, maps the design to Godot idioms, and gives an incremental, behavior-preserving migration without introducing heavier AI architectures.
assertions: Recommends an explicit state machine (State pattern, enum-based FSM or state nodes) to replace the independent boolean flags
Explains that entry/exit or transition handling resets dash state and timers when hurt interrupts a dash, fixing the stuck-dash bug
Maps the design to Godot idioms (for example enum + match, Node or RefCounted state objects, signals, InputMap actions, _physics_process delegation)
Proposes an incremental migration that keeps the game working (one state or slice at a time, behavior preserved, playtested or tested per step)
Handles double jump as a counter or data inside an airborne state (or equivalent) rather than another independent boolean
Distinguishes applying a jump impulse from entering the airborne or ascending state, so a second jump while already rising works
Does not recommend heavier architectures such as behavior trees, GOAP, ECS or a global event bus for the player controller

evals.expected_output: A design review that flags speculative generality (factory hierarchy and provider for one product, an event bus hiding a single direct call, a global config singleton), keeps only abstractions with a real boundary (the repository test seam and a notification port around the external provider), points out the concrete defects introduced by the indirection (unawaited async handler errors, hidden dependencies, hard-to-test singleton), proposes a simpler wiring through constructor injection at a composition root, and does not add new patterns.
assertions: Flags the factory hierarchy and provider (AbstractNotificationSenderFactory, EmailNotificationSenderFactory, NotificationSenderFactoryProvider) as speculative for a single product and recommends removing or collapsing it
Keeps the IOrderRepository seam and a notification sender interface around SendGrid as justified boundaries instead of removing every abstraction
Identifies that EventBus.emit calls the async handler without awaiting it, so email failures become unhandled or silently lost
Identifies the Config singleton as hidden global state that hurts testability and recommends passing configuration or dependencies explicitly (constructor injection or a composition root)
Recommends replacing the event bus hop with a direct, explicit call or injected dependency for the single listener
Distinguishes a committed order from a failed notification: does not make placeOrder report failure or encourage retrying the whole order after the save succeeded
Does not require introducing additional patterns or infrastructure (new abstraction layers, plugin systems, message brokers) as the fix; reliability ideas such as an outbox are at most conditional

evals.prompt: Estoy haciendo un juego de sigilo en Roblox. Tendré unos 20-30 guardias NPC por servidor. Tienen que: patrullar entre waypoints, perseguir al jugador cuando lo ven, buscarlo en la última posición conocida si lo pierden, avisar a guardias cercanos para que acudan y huir a curarse cuando tienen poca vida. Más adelante queremos añadir guardias con linterna, perros y un jefe con fases. ¿Qué arquitectura de IA me recomiendas y cómo la organizo en scripts? Quiero que sea fácil añadir comportamientos nuevos sin que todo se vuelva un spaghetti.
evals.expected_output: Compares candidate AI architectures against the stated scale and growth, recommends a fitting one with clear reasons (not a planner by default), separates perception/knowledge from decisions, models guard variants as data, and adapts the design to Roblox: server-side AI in ModuleScripts, a shared time-sliced update instead of one loop per NPC, tag-based discovery, connection cleanup, and no assumption of a built-in behavior tree.
assertions: Compares at least two AI architectures (for example FSM/HFSM, behavior tree, utility AI) against the stated needs before recommending one
Does not recommend GOAP or HTN planning as the primary architecture for this scope
Separates perception or shared knowledge (blackboard, memory or alert data) from decision logic
Runs AI on the server in ModuleScripts and uses a shared, time-sliced or budgeted update rather than one loop or thread per NPC
Handles stale asynchronous work, such as discarding outdated pathfinding results or expired alerts, so guards do not act on obsolete information
Addresses cleanup of connections or resources when an NPC is removed (Disconnect, Destroying, Maid, Trove or Janitor)
Models guard variants (flashlight guards, dogs, boss) through data, configuration or composition rather than a deep class hierarchy

evals.prompt: En Unity 6 quiero un sistema de buffs y debuffs para enemigos (veneno, ralentización, escudo, furia). Los stats base de cada tipo de enemigo están en ScriptableObjects (`EnemyStats`: vida, velocidad, daño, armadura) que comparten todos los enemigos de ese tipo. Los efectos se apilan: algunos suman un valor fijo, otros un porcentaje y otros multiplican, y tienen duración. La barra de vida y los iconos de estado de cada enemigo deben actualizarse cuando cambian sus stats. Habrá hasta ~80 enemigos a la vez. Diséñame la arquitectura y dame el código base en C#.
evals.expected_output: A proportional design that keeps shared ScriptableObject data read-only and computes per-instance runtime stats, applies modifiers in an explicit stage order with source tracking and expiry, recomputes lazily when modifiers change, wires per-enemy UI through owned subscriptions that are removed on disable or destroy, and avoids global managers, event buses or ECS for this scale.
assertions: Never mutates the shared EnemyStats ScriptableObject at runtime; keeps per-instance runtime stats or modifier state separate from the shared asset and says why
Defines an explicit, deterministic modifier order (for example flat, then additive percent, then multiplicative) instead of applying effects in arrival order
Tracks modifier source or identity so a specific buff can be removed or refreshed, and handles duration expiry
Recomputes or caches final stats only when modifiers change (dirty flag or event-driven recompute) rather than rebuilding every frame for every enemy
Per-enemy UI subscribes to that enemy's change notification and unsubscribes in OnDisable or OnDestroy (or equivalent owned lifetime)
Does not introduce a global event bus, singleton manager or ECS/DOTS for ~80 enemies

evals.prompt: Our match service (Node.js) calls the inventory service over HTTP (`POST /grants`) to give players their rewards when a match ends. Sometimes the call times out and players complain they did not get their rewards, so I want to add retries. A teammate suggested wrapping the call with `axios-retry` (3 retries, exponential backoff). Is that enough? How should we do this properly?
evals.expected_output: Explains that a timeout does not mean the grant failed, so naive retries can double-grant; requires an idempotency key per match/player reward that the inventory service enforces; keeps bounded backoff with jitter at a single layer with a deadline; optionally makes the grant durable (outbox or queue) if rewards must survive crashes; avoids adding heavy infrastructure without need.
assertions: Explains that a timeout does not prove the grant failed, so blind retries can grant rewards twice
Requires an idempotency key derived from the match and player (or reward id) that the inventory service stores and enforces
Keeps retries bounded with exponential backoff plus jitter and an overall deadline, and retries only transient failures
Warns against stacking retries at several layers (client library, service code, gateway) that multiply attempts
Mentions making the grant durable (outbox, queue or persisted pending grant with reconciliation) only as needed if rewards must survive crashes, not as a mandatory first step
Does not recommend unrelated heavy infrastructure such as a saga orchestrator, event sourcing or a service mesh for this fix

evals.prompt: Estoy empezando un roguelike pequeño en Godot 4.3, lo hago yo solo y quiero terminarlo en unos 3 meses. Necesito inventario, guardar y cargar partida, y que la UI reaccione cuando cambia la vida o el oro del jugador. Quiero hacerlo bien desde el principio para no tener que rehacerlo después. ¿Qué arquitectura y patrones me recomiendas?
evals.expected_output: A deliberately lightweight structure sized to a solo three-month project: plain data or Resources for items, signals for UI reactions, a small number of autoloads with clear ownership, an explicit versioned save format rather than serializing nodes, the shared-Resource mutation caveat, and explicit triggers for adding more structure later.
assertions: Explicitly scales the architecture to a solo, three-month project and pushes back on building for hypothetical future needs
Uses Godot signals (or equivalent native mechanism) for UI reactions to health or gold changes instead of polling or a custom global event bus framework
Warns that shared Resources are shared across instances (mutating one affects all users) and recommends duplicate() or resource_local_to_scene or separate runtime state for mutable data
Recommends an explicit save format (dictionary or DTO with a version field) rather than serializing nodes or the whole scene tree
Limits autoloads or global singletons to a few with clear ownership and warns against autoload god objects
Names at least one concrete trigger for when to add more structure later (revisit trigger)
Does not recommend layering several heavy patterns at once (DI container, service locator, repository, ECS, plugin architecture) for this scope
